source.title: The Hidden Evolution of Disguised Visual Context inside the VLM
source.authors: Wish Suharitdamrong; Tony Alex; Xiatian Zhu; Muhammad Awais; Sara Atito

record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures image–text representation alignment inside VLMs, using PCA visualizations rather than distances between independently trained models.
record.gate_note: The paper directly reports whether image-token and text-token representations converge across layers for three integration architectures. The representation analysis uses only the Qwen2.5-Instruct-0.5B backbone trained on LLaVA-NeXT. It does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or performance, or compare independently trained vision and language models. CKA results concern within-modality changes across layers, and frequency, attention, benchmark, and filtering results do not themselves measure the claim’s cross-model alignment.
record.test_reason: No version of the claim is tested. The study projects image-token and text-token hidden states from a single VLM (Qwen2.5-0.5B with SigLIP2, jointly fine-tuned) into a shared 3D PCA space and inspects them layer by layer. This is a within-model modality-gap question across depth, under three integration architectures. It does not compare representations of independently trained models (V1, V3–V5). It does not pair images with their captions or relate alignment to model quality (V2). It does not vary the similarity measure for cross-model convergence (V6). The evidence is qualitative PCA with no alignment number. The CKA analysis compares layers within one model, not models with each other. The finding is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim that IN-CT's higher-frequency visual features, confirmed causally by low-pass filtering, drive its advantage on text-centric and OCR tasks. They attribute the representational differences to architecture rather than training budget.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses qualitative shared-space PCA visualizations of image and text tokens within VLMs across layers, rather than measuring similarity between independently trained models or testing convergence against model scale and capability.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported cross-modal alignment changes with integration architecture: IN-CT converges, while LW-AT and LW-GC remain separated.

fits_no_version.finding: In-context injection makes image and text tokens inside one VLM merge into a shared PCA region by the final layers. Under both layer-wise injection designs (LW-AT, LW-GC) they stay separated at every depth. The evidence is qualitative and covers only Qwen2.5-0.5B trained on LLaVA-NeXT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a VLM, whether visual tokens converge toward the language-token subspace across depth depends on the integration architecture (in-context versus layer-wise injection).

record.problems: The alignment evidence is qualitative PCA rather than a reported numerical cross-modal similarity measure. The representation analysis covers only one backbone size and one instruction-tuning mixture, and does not test alignment against model capability or scale.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows bearing on the claim were omitted. The paper reports other analyses, including CKA across layers, Fourier frequency characteristics, attention mass, benchmark outcomes, and a frequency-filter intervention; these do not directly measure the claim’s cross-model or cross-modal alignment behavior.

untested.parts: all: no cross-model alignment across scale, architecture or objective
all: no independent vision and language models, no image-caption pairing, no alignment versus model quality
all: no cross-model alignment level, plateau, or test of its causes

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2 'tests' verdict and its V2/V7 labels are withdrawn. The reader's guess has two problems. First, a modality gap measured across layers within one jointly trained VLM is not the cross-model convergence that V2 describes. Second, no alignment metric is computed. The benchmark results across backbones from 0.5B to 7B concern task performance, not representational alignment.

versions.untested_parts: No representation-alignment measurements across model sizes, capabilities, architectures, or independently trained models.

The study measures image and text token representations within VLMs across layers, not independent vision and language models on paired image-caption data; it does not test alignment as both models improve or scale.
No comparison of seeds, learned features, or shared subspaces across independently initialized networks.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No comparison of cross-model convergence under alternative similarity metrics, metric settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.

The study shows architecture-dependent alignment, but does not quantify whether alignment is far from complete or plateaus, or test shared data/objectives against a common model of reality as explanations.

rows.subject: IN-CT (Qwen2.5-Instruct-0.5B, LLaVA-NeXT)
rows.stage_stated: LLaVA-NeXT instruction tuning; full-parameter instruction tuning
rows.operation_detail: Project image and text hidden states into a shared 3D PCA space across layers and inspect their separation.
rows.measure: Qualitative image-token/text-token separation and convergence in shared 3D PCA space
rows.value: The image and text token clusters progressively merge into a shared representational space by the final layers.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes progressive convergence. This is an internal, across-layer VLM result, not a comparison of independent vision and language models or a scale sweep.
rows.check: Measures within-model, across-layer image/text token merging in a jointly trained VLM, judged visually from PCA. This is not alignment between independently trained vision and language models on image-caption pairs, nor alignment versus model quality. So it does not bear on V2, and it does not bear on V7's causes or plateau.

rows.subject: LW-AT (Qwen2.5-Instruct-0.5B, LLaVA-NeXT)
rows.stage_stated: LLaVA-NeXT instruction tuning; full-parameter instruction tuning
rows.operation_detail: Project image and text hidden states into a shared 3D PCA space across layers and inspect their separation.
rows.measure: Qualitative image-token/text-token separation and convergence in shared 3D PCA space
rows.value: Image representations remain separated from the text cluster at every depth.
rows.note: The paper explicitly reports no convergence for this integration architecture.
rows.check: Same construct mismatch as r1. The LW-AT separation is a property of the layer-wise injection design (tokens never pass through the residual stream), not evidence about cross-model convergence.
